evidence: keyfile-and-locks-rendered: manifests/gnome_lock_screen.pp:63-75 render [org/gnome/desktop/session] idle-delay=uint32 ${screenlock_timeout_seconds} (5*60=300 at defaults, line 9) and [org/gnome/desktop/screensaver] lock-enabled=true, lock-delay=uint32 ${screenlock_grace_seconds} (0); the probe cats the keyfile and the locks file (80-89) and the expect matches exactly that text; supported (my applied run printed it verbatim)

a-user-cannot-override-the-locked-keys: manifests/gnome_lock_screen.pp:80-92 lock the three keys, so a user write to them must be refused while an unlocked key stays writable, and the action tests exactly that; mutates declares everything the action changes (dconf-service, p8testdesk, its user db, /run/p8test-dconf). But the read-only effect, cat /run/p8test-dconf/user.txt, is the action's own stdout (its echo of 'refused'/'written' from dconf write's exit status, plus reads taken inside the action), redirected to a file, not an independent observation of the action's result. The result is observable read-only: e.g. reading p8testdesk's user database with a user-db-only profile (DCONF_PROFILE holding just user-db:user) would show the three keys absent and text-scaling-factor 1.25. Derivation failure under the mutates rule (the effect must show the action's result, not the action's own output)

compiled-db-serves-the-policy: manifests/gnome_lock_screen.pp:94-98 declare the refreshonly '/usr/bin/dconf update' that compiles /etc/dconf/db/local (notified by 63-78); dconf read with DCONF_PROFILE=user reads the compiled database and the expect (uint32 300, true, uint32 0) is what the defaults produce. The mismatch varies only the profile name (a missing profile has no system-db:local, so the values cannot come from the compiled db; it printed empty and failed as required); supported
